name: Burmese hsaing waing (drum-circle ensemble)
lineage: Burmese hsaing waing percussion-led ensemble tradition, the canonical Burmese folk-and-ceremonial instrumental form. The ensemble centers on the pat waing tuned-drum-circle (twenty-one tuned drums arranged in a horseshoe around the seated lead player) plus kyi waing tuned-gong-circle, hne double-reed shawm, chauk lon bat double-headed drum-pair, si small cymbals, and wa wooden-clappers. The pat waing drum-circle player is the de-facto ensemble leader, with the player simultaneously delivering melodic, rhythmic, and ensemble-cueing functions. Performance contexts span weddings, religious-festival celebrations, theatrical accompaniment (zat pwe), and the classical mahagita repertoire performance. Distinguished from neighboring Thai pi phat and Khmer pinpeat ensembles by Burmese hsaing waing's tuned-drum-circle (vs gong-circle-led) instrumental hierarchy.
